# Copper Scroll Column 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 3Q15 (Cave 3), Col. 7 | **Condition:** Corroded in places; mostly legible

---

**7:1** In the tomb in the ravine at Kippah,

**7:2** along the route from Beth Tamar to Hebron:

**7:3** seven cubits down —

**7:4** thirty-two talents.

**7:5** In the cave at the old burial site of Abel-Shittim,

**7:6** out in the field:

**7:7** four cubits down —

**7:8** six gold bars.

**7:9** In the underground passage at Horon,

**7:10** in the field:

**7:11** five and a half

**7:12** talents.

**7:13** In the irrigation ditch at [...]

**7:14** tithe vessels

**7:15** of the lord of the nations —

**7:16** all of it is sabbatical-year tithe;

**7:17** the other seventh has been made impure.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The geographical sweep of Column 7 is remarkable — from Abel-Shittim east of the Jordan to Hebron deep in the Judean highlands. Someone was caching treasure across an enormous swath of territory. The sabbatical-year tithe reference reflects the agricultural sabbath of Leviticus 25 — every seventh year the land was to rest and all produce was common property. That even this tithe was systematically catalogued shows the bureaucratic thoroughness of the scroll's authors.*
